chunks: From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from 'Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had three wives, and he married two more to them in a single contract, then consummated the marriage with one of them, and then he died. He said: 'If he consummated with the wife whose name he mentioned first at the time of the marriage contract, then her marriage is valid, she inherits, and she observes the waiting period.' He said: 'And if he consummated with the one mentioned after the first, then her marriage is invalid, she does not inherit, but she keeps what she took of the dowry because she made his private part permissible to her, and she observes the waiting period.'
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided when a man marries multiple women in one contract and dies after consummating with only one?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the Shia juristic principle of 'explicit mention' (dhikr) in determining the validity of simultaneous marriages, distinguishing between the first wife whose name was specified at the time of contract and the second whose status remains ambiguous. It establishes that while the first wife retains full inheritance rights, the second wife’s marriage is void yet she keeps her dowry (sadaq) as compensation for consummation, reflecting the Imami emphasis on precise contractual intent. This ruling underscores the importance of clear designation in polygamous unions to prevent legal uncertainty regarding inheritance and waiting periods (iddah).
